review_notes: I read the whole file. It is generated certificate code with no simp attributes or simp lemmas. Its only simp calls are `simp_rw [sums_eq]` (4 times) and `simpa only [...]` (4 times). `sums_eq : chunk j i = sums j i` rewrites toward the cached table and cannot loop, because `sums` does not unfold to `chunk`. The one weakness in the simp interface is the bridge lemma `tableRule_contains_bridge` in TableRuleBridge.lean. Its conclusion uses `(if b then 1 else 0)` with a variable Bool `b`, so every concrete use needs the same ad hoc `simpa only` cleanup list. I did not compile anything, so I cannot say whether the proposed bridge restatement or the `Bool.false_eq_true` entry is needed.

findings.problem: `tableRule_contains_bridge` states its conclusion with a generic `(if b then 1 else 0)` and a generic cast of `m`. The bridge lemma has no specialisations for `b = false` and `b = true` and no simp-normal form for them. So every instance has to be cleaned up with the same hand-written `simpa only` list (`Nat.cast_ofNat`, `Nat.cast_zero`, `Nat.cast_one`, `Bool.false_eq_true`, `ite_false`, `ite_true`). The identical list appears four times, at lines 341, 679, 1017 and 1355. The list is brittle: any change to the shape of the bridge statement or to how the `ite` on `Bool` normalises breaks all four call sites.
findings.proposed_change: Move the normalisation into TableRuleBridge.lean. Either state the bridge with a form that needs no simp, for example an exponent or index given by `b.toNat` or a `cond`-free statement. Or add two specialised corollaries, `tableRule_contains_bridge_false` and `tableRule_contains_bridge_true`, whose conclusions are already `tableMomentRule a m 0` and `tableMomentRule a m 1`. Their proofs would use `simpa only [...]` once. The call sites here would then be `rw [← checked]; exact tableRule_contains_bridge_false ...`.
findings.benefit: The simp-lemma list lives in one place instead of four copies. Concrete uses no longer depend on `Nat.cast`, `ite` and `Bool` normalisation behaving a particular way, and the call sites become shorter and easier to read.
